neighbours.label: The analyte name in a clinical blood-test measurement, right before 'levels' (serum ferritin levels, vitamin D levels), vs medical sentences that mention blood tests without a measured analyte level
fire: The nurse ordered a test to check her serum magnesium levels.
Patients with anaemia often have low plasma ferritin levels.
High homocysteine levels have been linked to stroke.
The doctor said his blood urea levels were slightly raised.
Researchers measured serum calcium levels in every volunteer.
Low vitamin B12 levels can cause tingling in the hands.
The trial tracked plasma cortisol levels before and after exercise.
Her thyroid hormone levels returned to normal within a month.
quiet: The nurse ordered a test to check her heart rhythm overnight.
Patients with anaemia often feel tired and short of breath.
High blood pressure has been linked to stroke.
The doctor said his kidney scan looked slightly unusual.
Researchers measured the height and weight of every volunteer.
Low back pain can cause trouble sleeping at night.
The trial tracked heart rate before and after exercise.
Her thyroid gland returned to its normal size within a month.

predictions: 'serum/plasma/blood <analyte> levels' 0.25-0.5 on the analyte; matched medical sentences without an analyte-level phrase under 0.12.
notes: Card: peaks on analyte pieces before ' levels' (homocyste|ine, triglycer|ide, sodium, B1|2, ure|a) and 'less than' before a count. Probe: 'serum ferrit|in levels' 0.400, 'Low vitamin D levels' 0.321, 'High cholesterol levels' 0.114, 'blood sugar was high' 0.136; 'elevated levels of potassium' only 0.053 (analyte after 'levels'), 'Water levels' 0.033, 'difficulty levels' 0.001. Fire items put the analyte right before 'levels'.
